data.content_ref: inline:The target's claim that the dilemma 'dissolves' is directly contradicted by its own enumerated counterconditions. The mechanism asserts action follows because 'all alternatives have been eliminated,' but the first countercondition explicitly admits that multiple unrefuted theories may remain, in which case elimination does not yield a unique default. The eliminative-default story only dissolves the dilemma in the special case where exactly one theory survives; in the general case the agent still faces a choice the mechanism cannot arbitrate. Thus the claim overstates its scope: it does not dissolve the dilemma, it merely narrows it. Additionally, the mechanism's conclusion that 'the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all' is a non sequitur — even granting that action defaults to unrefuted theories, the process by which theories were refuted (test severity, scope of criticism) determines which theories survive and therefore directly shapes the outcome.
